_about: The curriculum: thirty lessons in four levels, beginner to swinging, drafted by AI and marked so until Avi has read them. The order of the list is the order of the path (Lesson.path_order), tracks interleaved so no two lessons of one kind come in a row. Phrases list notes as [midi, beat, length] or [midi, beat, length, velocity]; the seed command turns them into the stored shape. Every exercise is in its chart's own key, rhythm motifs are written in straight counts and the judge swings them with the style's feel, and a model player passes every exercise through the real judge in tests/js/spri53.test.js. Voicings and comping are not here: that kind is not scored in version 1.

lessons.title: Chord tones on the beat
lessons.summary: Land on a note of the chord on the strong beats and the line sounds like it belongs.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

A chord is three or four notes that sound good together. C is C, E and G. Am is A, C and E. F is F, A and C. G7 is G, B, D and F. When the band moves to a chord, those are the notes it is playing, so those are the notes that are safe for you too.

The strong beats are the ones a listener feels: beat 1 most of all, then beat 3. Land on a chord tone there and almost anything you play in between will sound like you meant it.

## Hear

Press Hear. The phrase walks up and down the notes of each chord, one to a beat. It is plain, and it sounds settled, because every note belongs.

## Play

The chords are C, Am, F and G7, one to a bar. Before the take, find the notes of each chord on the keyboard. The Play screen names the chord of each bar and shows its notes. Start with beat 1 only, then add beat 3, then every beat.

Only the notes that fall on the beats the exercise names are judged. Between them you are free.

exercises.title: A chord tone on beat 1
exercises.instructions: Play one note per bar, on beat 1, and make it a note of that bar's chord: C is C E G, Am is A C E, F is F A C, G7 is G B D F. Any octave. Four bars, four notes.

exercises.title: Chord tones on beats 1 and 3
exercises.instructions: Two notes a bar now, on beat 1 and beat 3, each a note of the chord. Move to a different chord tone each time so it sings a little.

exercises.title: A chord tone on every beat
exercises.instructions: Four notes a bar, one on each beat, all chord tones. Walk up the chord, then down it, and change direction when the chord changes.

lessons.title: Rhythm motifs
lessons.summary: Pick a short rhythm and repeat it. A good rhythm makes any notes sound intentional.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

A motif is a short idea you repeat. A rhythm motif is the timing alone: which beats you play on, whatever notes you choose. Repeating it each bar gives the listener something to hold on to, and it is the quickest way to sound like you know what you are doing.

Beats are counted from 0 here: 0 is beat 1, 1 is beat 2, and 1.5 is the half beat after beat 2, the "and".

## Hear

Press Hear. Every bar plays the same rhythm: a long note on beat 1, then a short one on the "and" of 2. The notes change with the chords, the rhythm does not.

## Play

These exercises use a straight feel, so the "and" is exactly half way between beats. Match the rhythm in every bar. The notes are free, but play only the rhythm: an extra note is counted against you.

exercises.title: Beats 1 and 3
exercises.instructions: One note on beat 1 and one on beat 3 of every bar. Nothing else. Any notes.

exercises.title: Beat 1 and the and of 2
exercises.instructions: A note on beat 1, then a note half a beat after beat 2: count 1, 2 and. Repeat every bar.

exercises.title: Only on the ands
exercises.instructions: Four notes a bar, all on the ands: 1 and, 2 and, 3 and, 4 and. Do not play on a beat itself.

lessons.title: Scales that fit the chord
lessons.summary: Each chord has a scale that goes with it. Stay inside it and nothing clashes.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

A scale is the pool of notes that fit over a chord. Over Dm7 the pool is D dorian: D E F G A B C. Over G7 it is G mixolydian: G A B C D E F. Over Cmaj7 it is C major. In this key those are all the same seven white notes, which is why a two five one in C is a friendly place to start.

Staying in the scale is the first rule of improvising. The Play screen lights each note as you play: chord tones, scale tones, or outside.

## Hear

Press Hear. The phrase runs up and down the scales, a bar for each chord.

## Play

Play anything you like, but keep to the scale of the chord that is sounding. The score is the share of your notes that are chord or scale tones, so every wrong note costs you.

exercises.title: Stay in the scale
exercises.instructions: Four bars of any notes you like, as long as they fit the chord. Slow and steady is fine. Aim for a clean take.

exercises.title: One scale, two chords
exercises.instructions: Dm7 for two bars, then G7 for two bars. D dorian and G mixolydian are the same notes here, so stay inside the white keys and focus on the rhythm of what you play.

exercises.title: Scales round a turnaround
exercises.instructions: Cmaj7, Am7, Dm7, G7: one chord a bar and a different scale for each. Keep every note inside the scale of the chord that is sounding.

lessons.title: Chord tones through the blues
lessons.summary: Twelve bars, three chords, every one a seventh chord. The form every band knows.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

The twelve-bar blues is the most played form there is. In C it uses three chords: C7 for the home, F7 for the fourth, G7 for the fifth. Each is a seventh chord: a major triad with a flat seventh on top. C7 is C E G Bb. F7 is F A C Eb. G7 is G B D F.

The form is four bars of home (with a visit to F7 in bar 2 in some versions, not this one), two of F7, two of home, then G7, F7, home, G7. Learn where the changes fall and you can play the blues with anybody.

## Hear

Press Hear. Two chord tones a bar, on beats 1 and 3, all the way round the twelve bars. Follow the chord names on the chart as it plays.

## Play

Twelve bars is longer than anything so far, so count. Beat 1 only first, then beats 1 and 3, then every beat. The flat seventh is the blues note: make sure Bb, Eb and F get their turn.

exercises.title: The downbeat of every bar
exercises.instructions: Twelve bars. One note on beat 1 of each bar, a note of that bar's chord: C7 is C E G Bb, F7 is F A C Eb, G7 is G B D F. Watch for the change to F7 in bar 5 and to G7 in bar 9.

exercises.title: Beats 1 and 3 round the blues
exercises.instructions: Two chord tones a bar, on beats 1 and 3, for the whole twelve bars. Try the root on 1 and the seventh on 3 for a bar, then swap.

exercises.title: Walk the chord tones
exercises.instructions: A chord tone on every beat for twelve bars, like a walking bass line in your right hand. Up one bar, down the next, and land on a new chord's note the moment it changes.

lessons.title: Syncopation
lessons.summary: Put a note on the and, and leave the beat empty. The gap is what makes it groove.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

Syncopation is playing where the beat is not. A note on the "and" of 2, with nothing on beat 3, pulls the listener forward. The band keeps the beat for you, so you can afford to leave it empty.

The secret is to feel the beat you are not playing. Tap your foot on every beat and let the hands play between the taps.

## Hear

Press Hear. Every bar is the same: a note on 1, a note on the and of 2, and a note on 4. Beat 3 is silent, and the bar still feels complete.

## Play

Three rhythms, each with one note off the beat. Keep the pattern exact in every bar and do not fill the gaps. Any notes you like; the chords are C, G, Am and F.

exercises.title: 1, 2, and the and of 3
exercises.instructions: A note on beat 1, a note on beat 2, then a note on the and of 3. Nothing on 3 itself and nothing on 4. Repeat in every bar.

exercises.title: 1, the and of 2, and 4
exercises.instructions: A note on beat 1, a note on the and of 2, a note on beat 4. Count 1, 2 and, 4. Beat 3 stays empty.

exercises.title: Push into the next bar
exercises.instructions: A note on 1, a note on the and of 2, then a note on the and of 4 that pushes into the next bar. Keep your foot on the beat while the hand plays off it.

lessons.title: Call and response
lessons.summary: Hear a short phrase, answer it back. The oldest way to build a solo.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

Improvising is a conversation. You play a short phrase, then answer it. The answer keeps the rhythm of the call and follows its shape: if the call goes up, the answer goes up. It does not have to use the same notes.

This is how a good solo gets built out of nothing. Play something small, answer it, and you already have two bars of music.

## Hear

Press Hear. The call is in bar 1, the answer in bar 2. Same rhythm, same direction, different notes.

## Play

The exercise gives you the call to play yourself in one bar, and the answer is the bar you are scored on. Match the rhythm of the call and the way it moves. The last exercise asks for the same notes, in any octave.

exercises.title: Echo the rhythm
exercises.instructions: In bar 1 play C, D, E on beats 1, 2, 3. In bar 2 answer: three notes on the same beats, going up the same way. Any notes you like.

exercises.title: Answer a skip
exercises.instructions: In bar 2 play C on beat 1, a jump up to E on the and of 2, D on beat 3 and C on beat 4. In bar 3 answer with the same rhythm and the same up then down shape.

exercises.title: Echo the exact notes
exercises.instructions: In bar 3 play G, A, C, A on beats 1 to 4. In bar 4 answer with the same notes at the same beats. Any octave counts.

lessons.title: Chord tones in a two five one
lessons.summary: Dm7, G7, Cmaj7: the movement jazz is made of, and four notes to each chord.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

The two five one is the most common movement in jazz. In C it is Dm7, G7, Cmaj7: the second, fifth and first chords of the key. Each has four notes now. Dm7 is D F A C. G7 is G B D F. Cmaj7 is C E G B.

You already know chord tones on the beat. The new thing is that these chords share notes: the C of Dm7 is still there over Cmaj7, the F of Dm7 is still there over G7. Hold a note across a change when you can, and move only when you must.

## Hear

Press Hear. The phrase walks the four notes of each chord, one to a beat, and lands on the two notes that outline Cmaj7.

## Play

Beat 1 only, then beats 1 and 3, then every beat. Find the four notes of each chord before the take; the Play screen shows them for each bar. Between the named beats you are free.

exercises.title: A chord tone on beat 1
exercises.instructions: One note per bar, on beat 1, from that bar's chord: Dm7 is D F A C, G7 is G B D F, Cmaj7 is C E G B. Any octave.

exercises.title: Chord tones on beats 1 and 3
exercises.instructions: Two notes a bar, on beats 1 and 3, each a note of the chord. Try keeping a note that both chords share, then move by a step when the chord asks you to.

exercises.title: A chord tone on every beat
exercises.instructions: Four notes a bar, all chord tones, up one chord and down the next. The last two bars are both Cmaj7, so use them to come to rest.

lessons.title: Guide tones: thirds and sevenths
lessons.summary: The third and the seventh say what a chord is. Connect them across the changes.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

The root and the fifth do not tell you much. The third says major or minor, and the seventh says what kind of seventh. Those two are the guide tones.

The trick is that they move by a step into the next chord. In a two five one in C, the seventh of Dm7 (C) falls a half step to the third of G7 (B). The seventh of G7 (F) falls a half step to the third of Cmaj7 (E). A line of guide tones is smooth, and it spells out the harmony without a single other note.

## Hear

Press Hear. The phrase plays only thirds and sevenths. Listen to the half-step falls at each chord change.

## Play

Play only the third and the seventh of each chord. At each change, aim to land within a step of where you were. The score gives a point for each guide tone and a point for each change where you connect.

exercises.title: Find the thirds and sevenths
exercises.instructions: Play only thirds and sevenths. Dm7: F and C. G7: B and F. Cmaj7: E and B. Do not worry about connecting yet.

exercises.title: Connect the changes
exercises.instructions: Same notes, but now the last note of each bar and the first of the next must be guide tones a step apart: C down to B, then F down to E.

exercises.title: Guide tones round a longer path
exercises.instructions: Em7, A7, Dm7 G7, Cmaj7. Thirds and sevenths only, and look for the falls: D down to C sharp, then G down to F.

lessons.title: Approach notes
lessons.summary: Step in from a half step away and the target note sounds like an arrival.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

An approach note is a note a half step above or below a target, played just before it. It is not in the scale, and that is the point: it creates a small tension that the target resolves. A target is a chord tone you land on a strong beat.

It works because the ear expects the half step to move on. Play B flat then B, or E flat then E, and the second note feels like home.

## Hear

Press Hear. Listen for the short note a half step away, just before the chord tone it leads into.

## Play

Pick a chord tone to land on, and play the note a half step below or above it just before. The score counts the targets you reach this way. A target you land on without an approach does not count, and an approach that leads nowhere does not count either.

exercises.title: Approach the downbeat
exercises.instructions: Aim at a chord tone on beat 1 of each bar and play the note a half step below or above it on the beat before. You can also use the last half beat of the bar before.

exercises.title: Approach beats 1 and 3
exercises.instructions: Two targets a bar now, on beats 1 and 3. Mix approaches from above and below so it does not sound mechanical.

exercises.title: Approach notes at pace
exercises.instructions: Em7, A7, Dm7 G7, Cmaj7 at a moving tempo. Target beat 1 of every bar with a half-step approach.

lessons.title: When the scale changes
lessons.summary: One chord brings one new note. Find it before the bar arrives.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

In the first scales lesson every chord used the white keys. Real tunes are not so kind: a chord from outside the key brings a new note with it, and the scale that fits that chord has to change.

Over Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7 you are in C. The A7 that follows wants A mixolydian: A B C# D E F# G. Two new notes, C sharp and F sharp, and the C sharp is the one the ear hears, because it is the third of the chord. Over a Bb chord in the key of C, the scale is Bb major: B flat and E flat come in. Over a dominant seventh chord, mixolydian: the flat seventh of that chord.

## Hear

Press Hear. Three bars of white keys, then the A7 bar brings in C sharp and F sharp. Listen for the moment the colour changes.

## Play

The score is the share of your notes inside the scale of the chord that is sounding. Know the new note before the bar comes, so you reach for it on purpose.

exercises.title: The A7 bar
exercises.instructions: Dm7, G7, Cmaj7, A7, round and round. White keys for three bars, then A mixolydian for the A7 bar: A B C sharp D E F sharp G. Make the C sharp heard.

exercises.title: The B flat bar
exercises.instructions: C, Bb, F, C. The Bb bar wants Bb major: Bb C D Eb F G A. Two flats, and the B natural you were playing a bar ago is now wrong.

exercises.title: Three mixolydians round the blues
exercises.instructions: Twelve bars. C mixolydian over C7 (with B flat), F mixolydian over F7 (with E flat), G mixolydian over G7 (with F). Change scale the moment the chord changes.

lessons.title: Bossa rhythms
lessons.summary: A rhythm that sits across the bar line, over a two five one that swings nothing.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

Bossa nova is straight eighths, no swing, and its melodies live off the beat. The classic shape puts a note on 1, a note on the and of 2, and a note on 4, and the next bar answers with the ands. Play it light and let the band carry the pulse.

The chords are a two five one with an A7 at the end to send it round again, so you can keep your chord tones and guide tones in mind while the rhythm does the work.

## Hear

Press Hear. Every bar is the same rhythm: 1, the and of 2, and 4. The notes come from the chord of each bar.

## Play

Three rhythms, each more off the beat than the last. The notes are free, the rhythm is not: an extra note counts against you. Tap your foot through the whole take.

exercises.title: 1, the and of 2, and 4
exercises.instructions: The basic bossa shape in every bar: a note on 1, a note on the and of 2, a note on 4. Nothing on 3.

exercises.title: The ands of 1 and 2, then 4
exercises.instructions: A note on the and of 1, a note on the and of 2, then a note on beat 4. The first beat of the bar is silent: let the band play it.

exercises.title: Across the bar line
exercises.instructions: 1, the and of 2, 4, and the and of 4. Four notes a bar, the last one leaning into the next bar. Keep it even and quiet.

lessons.title: Guide tones round the turnaround
lessons.summary: Four chords, two guide tones each, and a line that never jumps.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

A turnaround is the four-chord loop that sends a tune back to the top: Cmaj7, Am7, Dm7, G7. Each chord has its third and its seventh. Cmaj7: E and B. Am7: C and G. Dm7: F and C. G7: B and F.

Watch how they connect. The B of Cmaj7 rises a half step to the C of Am7. The G of Am7 falls a step to the F of Dm7. The C of Dm7 falls a half step to the B of G7. The F of G7 falls a half step to the E of Cmaj7. Four chords, and the line moves by a step every time.

## Hear

Press Hear. Two notes a bar, nothing but guide tones, and every change is a step.

## Play

Thirds and sevenths only. The score gives a point for each guide tone and a point for each change where the two notes either side are a step apart. The third exercise adds an A7 that wants C sharp.

exercises.title: Find them round the turnaround
exercises.instructions: Cmaj7, Am7, Dm7, G7. Play only thirds and sevenths: E and B, C and G, F and C, B and F. Two notes a bar is plenty.

exercises.title: Connect every change
exercises.instructions: Same chords, and now the last note before each change and the first after it must be a step apart: B to C, G to F, C to B, F to E.

exercises.title: Guide tones with an A7
exercises.instructions: Dm7, G7, Cmaj7, A7. The A7 has C sharp and G as its guide tones. From the B of Cmaj7, C sharp is a step up; from the G of A7, F of Dm7 is a step down.

lessons.title: Answer with the shape
lessons.summary: Longer calls, a skip or two inside them, and an answer that follows every turn.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

The shape of a phrase is where it goes: up, down, up again. An answer that follows the shape sounds like a reply even when the notes are all different, and that is what makes a solo sound like one voice instead of a list of licks.

The calls here are longer, with four or five notes and a skip in the middle. Sing the call in your head before you answer it.

## Hear

Press Hear. The call rises and falls in bar 1; the answer in bar 2 rises and falls the same way on other notes.

## Play

Play the call in its bar, then answer in the next. The score counts the onsets you match and each turn of the shape you follow. The last exercise wants the exact notes, in any octave.

exercises.title: Up, up, then back
exercises.instructions: In bar 1 play A, C, E, D on beats 1 to 4. In bar 2 answer with four notes on the same beats that go up, up, then down. Any notes.

exercises.title: A call with eighth notes
exercises.instructions: In bar 2 play E on 1, D on the and of 1, C on 2, A on 3, C on 4. In bar 3 answer with the same rhythm: down, down, down, then up.

exercises.title: Echo five exact notes
exercises.instructions: In bar 3 play E on 1, F on 2, G on the and of 2, A on 3, C on 4. In bar 4 answer with the same notes on the same beats, any octave.

lessons.title: Approach notes through the blues
lessons.summary: Lead into the downbeat of every blues chord from a half step away.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

The blues lives on approach notes. The flat third sliding into the third, the flat fifth into the fifth: those are the blue notes, and every one of them is a half step away from a chord tone. Here you aim them at the downbeat of every bar.

Over C7 your targets are C, E, G and Bb. Reach each one from a half step below or above: B into C, Eb into E, F# into G, A into Bb. Over F7 and G7 do the same with their notes.

## Hear

Press Hear. Four bars of the blues, and at the end of each bar a short note a half step away leads into the next downbeat.

## Play

Twelve bars, slowly at first. The score counts the downbeats you reach through an approach note. The third exercise uses an eight-bar blues that changes chord twice a bar near the end.

exercises.title: Into every downbeat
exercises.instructions: Twelve bars. Aim a chord tone at beat 1 of every bar and play its half-step neighbour just before it. Any approach you miss, let go and aim at the next bar.

exercises.title: Beats 1 and 3 round the blues
exercises.instructions: Two targets a bar, beats 1 and 3, for twelve bars. Use both directions: a half step below into the third, a half step above into the fifth.

exercises.title: The eight-bar blues
exercises.instructions: C7, G7, F7, F7, C7, G7, then two chords a bar: C7 F7 and C7 G7. Approach the downbeat of every bar with a half step. Keep your eye on the chart for the quick changes at the end.

lessons.title: Chord tones through the jazz blues
lessons.summary: The blues with jazz changes: two chords in a bar, and a chord tone on every one of them.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

The jazz blues keeps the twelve-bar shape and fills it with movement. Bar 4 has Gm7 then C7, a two five into the F7 of bar 5. Bar 6 is F diminished seventh. Bar 8 is A7 altered, pulling to the Dm7 of bar 9. Bars 11 and 12 are a turnaround: C7 A7, Dm7 G7.

When two chords share a bar, the first takes beats 1 and 2, the second beats 3 and 4. A chord tone on beat 3 now has to be a note of the second chord. The chart on the Play screen shows both.

## Hear

Press Hear. The first four bars: C7, F7, C7, then Gm7 and C7 sharing a bar. Four chord tones in every bar, and the fourth bar changes under your hands.

## Play

Beat 1 first, which is the first chord of each bar. Then beats 1 and 3, so the second chord in a shared bar gets its own note. Then every beat at tempo.

exercises.title: Downbeats of the jazz blues
exercises.instructions: Twelve bars, one chord tone on beat 1 of each. Mind bar 6 (Fdim7 is F Ab B D) and bar 8 (A7alt is A C# F G, with Bb above).

exercises.title: Both chords of a shared bar
exercises.instructions: Chord tones on beats 1 and 3. In bars 4, 11 and 12 the chord changes on beat 3, so the second note belongs to the second chord: C7 in bar 4, A7alt in bar 11, G7 in bar 12.

exercises.title: Walk the jazz blues
exercises.instructions: A chord tone on every beat for twelve bars at a medium swing. Think like a bass player: step through the chord, and arrive on a new note the moment the chord changes.

lessons.title: The minor two five one
lessons.summary: Three scales in four bars: locrian, altered, dorian. The sound of minor jazz.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

In a minor key the two five one is Dm7b5, G7alt, Cm7, and each chord asks for a different scale. Over Dm7b5, D locrian: D Eb F G Ab Bb C. Over G7alt, the altered scale: G Ab Bb B Db Eb F, every tension flattened or sharpened. Over Cm7, C dorian: C D Eb F G A Bb.

The altered scale is the strange one. Its notes are the G7 chord's tensions bent out of shape: flat nine, sharp nine, flat five, sharp five. It sounds wrong on its own and right the moment it lands on Cm7. Play it slowly and let your ear catch up.

## Hear

Press Hear. A bar of locrian, a bar of altered, then two bars settling into C dorian.

## Play

The score is the share of your notes inside the scale of the chord that is sounding, so think a bar ahead. The second exercise is a minor turnaround with two half-diminished chords; the third is the minor blues over twelve bars.

exercises.title: Locrian, altered, dorian
exercises.instructions: Dm7b5, G7alt, Cm7, Cm7. D locrian in bar 1, G altered in bar 2, C dorian in bars 3 and 4. Slowly, and name the scale to yourself as each bar comes.

exercises.title: The minor turnaround
exercises.instructions: Cm7, Am7b5, Dm7b5, G7alt. Dorian, then A locrian (A Bb C D Eb F G), then D locrian, then G altered. Four scales, one a bar.

exercises.title: The minor blues
exercises.instructions: Twelve bars: Cm7 for four, Fm7 for two, Cm7 for two, then Ab7, G7alt, Cm7, G7alt. Dorian over the minor sevenths, mixolydian over Ab7, altered over G7alt.

lessons.title: Guide tones through secondary dominants
lessons.summary: Eight bars where every other chord is a dominant from outside the key. The guide tones still connect.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

A secondary dominant is a seventh chord that points at a chord other than the home: E7 points at Am7, C7 at Fmaj7, D7 at G7. Each one brings a note from outside the key, and that note is almost always its third: G sharp in E7, B flat in C7, F sharp in D7.

The guide tones still move by a step, so a line of thirds and sevenths carries you through the strange chords without a jump. Cmaj7 to E7: E down to D. E7 to Am7: G sharp down to G. Am7 to C7: C down to B flat. C7 to Fmaj7: B flat down to A. Fmaj7 to D7: E up to F sharp. D7 to Dm7: C stays. Dm7 to G7: C down to B.

## Hear

Press Hear. Eight bars, two guide tones a bar, every change a step or a held note.

## Play

Thirds and sevenths only. Slow first, so you can find G sharp, B flat and F sharp in time. The third exercise is a circle of fifths through the key with a half-diminished chord and an altered dominant in it.

exercises.title: Find them, slowly
exercises.instructions: Cmaj7, E7, Am7, C7, Fmaj7, D7, Dm7 G7, Cmaj7. Thirds and sevenths only: E7 is G sharp and D, C7 is E and B flat, D7 is F sharp and C. Two notes a bar.

exercises.title: Connect through the dominants
exercises.instructions: Same eight bars at tempo. At every change the two notes either side must be a step apart or the same note. Bar 7 changes on beat 3: Dm7 then G7.

exercises.title: Round the circle of fifths
exercises.instructions: Cmaj7, Fmaj7, Bm7b5, E7alt, Am7, Dm7, G7, Cmaj7. Thirds and sevenths. Bm7b5 is D and A; E7alt is G sharp and D. Every root falls a fifth, and the guide tones barely move.

lessons.title: Funk rhythms
lessons.summary: Short notes, lots of air, and a rhythm that never lands where you expect.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

Funk is about the space between the notes. The rhythm section locks onto the one and everything else is placed against it: a note right after the downbeat, a note on the and of 2, silence where the ear expects sound. Keep the notes short and let the band fill the rest.

The chords are Cm7, F9, Cm7, Bb13. They barely move, which is the point: the harmony sits still and the rhythm does all the talking.

## Hear

Press Hear. Every bar is the same shape: 1, the and of 1, the and of 2, then 4. Short, dry, and in the pocket.

## Play

Three rhythms with eighth notes off the beat. Keep every note short. The notes are free; the rhythm is judged exactly and an extra note costs you. The last one never plays beat 1 at all.

exercises.title: 1, the and of 1, the and of 2, 4
exercises.instructions: Four notes a bar: beat 1, the and of 1, the and of 2, beat 4. Short notes. Nothing on 2 or 3.

exercises.title: 1, the and of 2, 3, the and of 4
exercises.instructions: Beat 1, the and of 2, beat 3, the and of 4. The last note pushes into the next bar; keep it short so the one still lands clean.

exercises.title: Never on the one
exercises.instructions: The and of 1, beat 2, the and of 3, beat 4. Beat 1 is silent in every bar: let the drums have it, and come in right after.

lessons.title: Approach notes at tempo
lessons.summary: Two targets a bar round the turnaround, and eight bars of changes at a real swing tempo.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

At a medium swing tempo there is no time to think about the approach note: it has to be in your hand before the beat comes. The way to get there is to know the target first. Pick the chord tone you are aiming at on beat 1 and on beat 3, and the approach note is simply its neighbour.

Over a turnaround the targets change every bar: E or B over Cmaj7, C or G over Am7, F or C over Dm7, B or F over G7. Say the target to yourself a beat early and play its neighbour on the way.

## Hear

Press Hear. Round the turnaround, each bar ending with a short note a half step from the downbeat it leads into.

## Play

Beats 1 and 3 round the turnaround, then eight bars through secondary dominants, then eight bars of bossa changes with two targets a bar. The score counts targets reached through an approach.

exercises.title: Beats 1 and 3 round the turnaround
exercises.instructions: Cmaj7, Am7, Dm7, G7. Two targets a bar, on beats 1 and 3, each reached from a half step above or below.

exercises.title: Through the secondary dominants
exercises.instructions: Cmaj7, E7, Am7, C7, Fmaj7, D7, Dm7 G7, Cmaj7. Approach the downbeat of every bar. The new notes (G sharp, B flat, F sharp) make good targets and good approaches both.

exercises.title: Eight bars of bossa, two targets a bar
exercises.instructions: Cmaj7, Dm7 G7, Em7 A7, Dm7 G7, Cmaj7, Fmaj7, Dm7 G7, Cmaj7. Beats 1 and 3, so in the shared bars the second target belongs to the second chord.

lessons.title: Longer calls
lessons.summary: Six-note calls with eighth notes, answered over a two five one that moves under you.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

A real phrase has eighth notes in it, and answering one means hearing six notes at once and giving them back a bar later while the chord has changed. That is the skill: keep the shape and the rhythm of the call in your head through a change of harmony.

The chords are Dm7, G7, Cmaj7, A7. When you answer in the G7 bar, the notes that fit have moved; follow the shape and let the chord tell you which notes.

## Hear

Press Hear. A six-note call over Dm7 with two pairs of eighth notes, and an answer over G7 that keeps the rhythm and the shape on the new chord's notes.

## Play

Play the call in its bar and answer in the next. The first two exercises score the rhythm and the shape; the last wants the exact notes, in any octave, on an A7 bar.

exercises.title: Six notes, two pairs of eighths
exercises.instructions: In bar 1 play F, G (on 1 and the and of 1), A on 2, C, B (on 3 and the and of 3), A on 4. In bar 2 answer with the same rhythm and shape over G7.

exercises.title: A leap, then a fall
exercises.instructions: In bar 2 play B on 1, D on 2, F on the and of 2, E on 3, C on 4, B on the and of 4. In bar 3 answer over Cmaj7: up, up, down, down, down, same rhythm.

exercises.title: Echo six exact notes
exercises.instructions: In bar 3 play E on 1, D on the and of 1, C on 2, B on the and of 2, A on 3, C on 4. In bar 4, over A7, give back the same six notes on the same beats, any octave.

lessons.title: Swing the eighths
lessons.summary: Swing makes the second eighth of a beat late. Wait for the and and the band's feel does the rest.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

Swing means the two eighth notes in a beat are not equal. The first is long and the second comes late, about two thirds of the way through the beat instead of half way. The band plays it that way, so the off-beat you count as 'and' lands later than you would expect.

That is the whole secret of the feel. A line that waits for the and sounds loose and easy; the same line on straight eighths sounds stiff over a swinging band.

## Hear

Press Hear. The phrase is written in plain eighths and it comes out swung, because the band's feel moves them. Tap your foot on the beats and listen to the ands sit late.

## Play

The patterns are counted straight: 1, the and of 1, and so on. Count them that way and let the band's swing place the and: wait for it. The judge knows the feel too, so a note on the late and is on time and a straight one is early. The last exercise is a blues shuffle, which swings deeper.

exercises.title: Two pairs of eighths
exercises.instructions: Four notes a bar: beat 1, the and of 1, beat 3, the and of 3. Count it straight, wait for the ands, and keep the second note of each pair short.

exercises.title: A swung line
exercises.instructions: Four eighth notes in a row, then rest: beat 1, the and of 1, beat 2, the and of 2. Beats 3 and 4 are silent. The ands are late, so the group leans forward.

exercises.title: The blues shuffle
exercises.instructions: Over a blues shuffle, eighth notes on beats 1, 2 and 3 and their ands: six notes a bar, nothing on beat 4. The swing is deeper here, nearly a triplet, so wait even longer for each and.

lessons.title: Chord tones round the circle
lessons.summary: Eight chords whose roots fall a fifth each bar, and the small steps that join their chord tones.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

The circle of fifths is the road most jazz tunes drive down: every chord's root falls a fifth, C, F, B, E, A, D, G, back to C. Each chord is a different colour, so a chord tone that works in one bar is wrong in the next.

The road has a trick that makes it easy to walk. The seventh of each chord sits a step above the third of the next one: B in Cmaj7 falls to A in Fmaj7, E falls to D, and so on. Follow that and the line moves by the smallest steps.

## Hear

Press Hear. Two chord tones a bar, falling along the circle, always a step or two from the last. It sounds like a line, not like a list of notes.

## Play

The chords are Cmaj7, Fmaj7, Bm7b5, E7alt, Am7, Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7, one to a bar. Read the next chord before you reach it. E7alt is E, G sharp and D, with F and C as the altered notes.

exercises.title: A chord tone on every downbeat
exercises.instructions: Eight bars, one chord tone on beat 1 of each. Cmaj7 is C E G B, Fmaj7 is F A C E, Bm7b5 is B D F A, E7alt is E G sharp D, Am7 is A C E G, Dm7 is D F A C, G7 is G B D F.

exercises.title: Beats 1 and 3 round the circle
exercises.instructions: Two notes a bar, on beats 1 and 3, both chord tones. Use the step trick: the seventh you leave on lands a step from the third of the next chord.

exercises.title: Walk the circle
exercises.instructions: A chord tone on every beat for eight bars. Think of a bass line that always knows the next chord: arrive on a new note the moment the chord changes.

lessons.title: Answer with the swing
lessons.summary: A call with an off-beat in it, answered a bar later with the same long and short of the eighths.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

A call that swings has to be answered with the same swing. Copying the notes is not enough: the answer has to keep the long and short of the eighths, the late ands, the little push at the end.

So listen for the rhythm first and the notes second. Count the call against the beat, say it to yourself as 'one, and, two', and then play it back in the next bar, over the new chord.

## Hear

Press Hear. A short call over Dm7 with an off-beat in it, and an answer over G7 with the same swing and the same shape on the new chord's notes.

## Play

Play the call in its bar and answer in the next one. The first two exercises score the rhythm and the shape; the last wants the exact notes, in any octave. Wait for the late ands and the answer lands on time.

exercises.title: Four notes and two late ones
exercises.instructions: In bar 1 play D on 1, F on the and of 2, A on 3, G on the and of 4. In bar 2 answer over G7 with the same rhythm and the same shape: up, up, then a step back.

exercises.title: A call that pushes
exercises.instructions: In bar 2 play G on 1, B on the and of 1, D on the and of 2, C on 3, A on 4, G on the and of 4. In bar 3 answer over Cmaj7 with the same rhythm and the same up and down.

exercises.title: Echo it note for note
exercises.instructions: In bar 3 play E on the and of 1, G on 2, C on the and of 2, B on 3, A on the and of 4. In bar 4 give back the same five notes on the same beats, any octave.

lessons.title: Scales when the key moves
lessons.summary: A backdoor ii V, a key change up a tone and a run of secondary dominants: new scales every bar or two.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

When a tune changes key, the scales change with it, and so do the notes that fit. Up a tone from C to E flat, the white keys stop working and three black keys take over: B flat, E flat and A flat.

You do not have to learn eight new scales. Name the chord, name its scale, play it. Fm7 is F dorian, B flat 7 is B flat mixolydian, E flat maj7 is E flat major. Same shapes as before, a tone higher.

## Hear

Press Hear. The line runs the scales of a ii V I in C, then the same ii V I a tone up. Listen for the moment the key slips, in bar 5.

## Play

Three charts where the ground moves: the backdoor, the key change, and a run of secondary dominants. Read one chord ahead, because the new scale has to be in your fingers on the downbeat.

exercises.title: The backdoor
exercises.instructions: Fm7, Bb7, Cmaj7, Cmaj7. F dorian, then B flat mixolydian, then C major. The first two chords borrow from C minor, so a few black keys appear for two bars.

exercises.title: Up a tone
exercises.instructions: Eight bars: Dm7, G7, Cmaj7, Cmaj7, then Fm7, Bb7, Ebmaj7, Ebmaj7. The white keys fit the first four bars, and the last four need B flat, E flat and A flat.

exercises.title: A scale for every dominant
exercises.instructions: Cmaj7, E7, Am7, C7, Fmaj7, D7, Dm7 G7, Cmaj7. Each dominant is mixolydian: E7 brings G sharp and C sharp, C7 brings B flat, D7 brings F sharp.

lessons.title: Guide tones through a tritone sub
lessons.summary: G7 swapped for D flat 7 shares its third and seventh, and the guide tones slide down by half steps.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

The tritone substitution swaps G7 for D flat 7. It sounds like a surprise but the guide tones tell you why it works: the third and seventh of D flat 7 are F and B (written C flat), the same two notes as the third and seventh of G7, swapped round.

Over Dm7, D flat 7 and Cmaj7 the top line falls by a half step, C, B, B, and the lower line holds F, F and then falls to E. A line like that is why the substitution is worth knowing.

## Hear

Press Hear. Two guide tones a bar. Listen to the top voice slide down a half step as the chord drops from D to D flat.

## Play

The first exercise is the substitution itself. Then the minor version, where the line falls again, and last the whole circle of fifths, where every seventh is a step above the next third. Thirds and sevenths only, and connect them.

exercises.title: The slide down
exercises.instructions: Dm7, Db7, Cmaj7, Cmaj7. Dm7: F and C. Db7: F and B. Cmaj7: E and B. The top voice falls C, B, B; the lower one holds F, F and then falls to E.

exercises.title: The minor version
exercises.instructions: Dm7b5, G7alt, Cm7, Cm7. Dm7b5: F and C. G7alt: B and F. Cm7: E flat and B flat. The top voice falls again, C, B, B flat, and the lower one ends on E flat.

exercises.title: Guide tones round the circle
exercises.instructions: Eight bars, Cmaj7 to Fmaj7 to Bm7b5 to E7alt to Am7 to Dm7 to G7 to Cmaj7. Thirds and sevenths only. The seventh you leave is a step from the third you arrive on, every time.

lessons.title: Comping rhythms
lessons.summary: The short chords a jazz pianist places off the beat: the Charleston and two rhythms that push the band.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

Comping is what you play behind a soloist, or behind yourself: short chords placed on rhythms that leave space. The classic jazz comping rhythms are a few simple shapes that sit just off the beat, and they only work swung.

The Charleston is a chord on 1 and a chord on the and of 2, and then silence. A chord that lands late on the and of 2 pulls the band forward, and the silence after it is what makes it swing.

## Hear

Press Hear. Short two-note chords on the Charleston, bar after bar of a C blues. The chords are plain; the placing is the point.

## Play

Play any chord or any note you like, short, on the beats of the pattern, and nothing else. The patterns are counted straight and the swing places the ands. The last one is the longest, twelve bars of jazz blues, so keep it steady.

exercises.title: The Charleston
exercises.instructions: A chord on beat 1 and a chord on the and of 2, in every bar. Short, then silence until the next bar. Wait for the late and.

exercises.title: Both ands
exercises.instructions: A chord on the and of 2 and a chord on the and of 4, in every bar. Nothing on the beats themselves: the band keeps them, and you land between.

exercises.title: Beat 1, the and of 2, 3, the and of 4
exercises.instructions: Four chords a bar: beat 1, the and of 2, beat 3, the and of 4. Twelve bars of jazz blues. Keep the chords short so the last one leans into the next bar and the one lands clean.

lessons.title: Approach notes with a swing
lessons.summary: Half steps on the late and, leaning into the target on the beat, round faster changes.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

An approach note is a half step that leans into a chord tone. At a medium swing tempo it lives on the and: the approach sits on the late and before the beat and the chord tone lands on the beat, so it sounds like a small slide into the chord.

Here the changes come faster and you do not have time to decide. Pick the target for the next bar while you play this one, and step in from below or above, whichever is nearer.

## Hear

Press Hear. Eighth-note approaches into the target of each bar, swung, round a iii vi ii V.

## Play

The chords are Em7, A7, Dm7 G7 and Cmaj7, then the jazz blues. Aim at beat 1 first, then at beats 1 and 3, and finish with the jazz blues at a brisk 130. If you miss an approach, let it go and aim at the next one.

exercises.title: Into every downbeat
exercises.instructions: Em7, A7, Dm7 G7, Cmaj7. Aim a chord tone at beat 1 of each bar and play its half-step neighbour on the and before it. A7 has C sharp, E and G to aim at.

exercises.title: Beats 1 and 3
exercises.instructions: Two targets a bar, beats 1 and 3. In the bar of Dm7 G7 the second target belongs to G7, so aim at B, D or F there.

exercises.title: Twelve bars of jazz blues
exercises.instructions: Approach the downbeat of every bar of the jazz blues at a brisk tempo. Bar 6 is Fdim7 and bar 8 is A7alt, so read ahead and choose your target before you get there.

lessons.title: Call and response over the blues
lessons.summary: A blues lick answered on the next chord, over a shuffle where the eighths swing hard.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

The blues is built on call and response, one phrase and then its answer, and it is shuffled: the eighths are swung hard, closer to a triplet than the jazz swing. The call says something and the answer repeats it, usually on the next chord.

Blues licks lean on the flat third and the flat fifth, the notes between the keys. You have the notes, so listen for the push and pull of the rhythm and let the shuffle carry it.

## Hear

Press Hear. A short blues lick over C7 and its answer a fourth up over F7, in the same shuffle.

## Play

The twelve-bar blues in C, at a shuffle. Play the call in its bar and answer in the next. The first two score the rhythm and the shape. The last wants the exact notes, in any octave, so say them to yourself before you play them back.

exercises.title: A short blues lick
exercises.instructions: In bar 1 over C7 play C on 1, E flat on the and of 1, F on 2, G on 3. In bar 2 answer over F7 with the same rhythm and shape, a fourth higher.

exercises.title: A climbing call
exercises.instructions: In bar 2 over F7 play F on 1, A flat on 2, B flat on the and of 2, B on 3, C on 4. In bar 3 answer over C7: same beats, same climb.

exercises.title: Echo the lick note for note
exercises.instructions: In bar 3 over C7 play G on 1, B flat on the and of 1, G on 2, E on 3, E flat on the and of 3, C on 4. In bar 4 give back the same six notes on the same beats, any octave.

lessons.title: Chord tones on 2 and 4
lessons.summary: A swing band feels beats 2 and 4. Land chord tones there and the line floats on the band.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

A swing band feels beats 2 and 4. The drummer's hi-hat closes there and the whole band leans on them, so a note placed on 2 or 4 sounds like it belongs to the band, while a note on 1 and 3 sounds like the start of a bar.

Play chord tones on 2 and 4 and the line floats on top of the band instead of sitting on it. It is the same skill as before, aimed at the other beats.

## Hear

Press Hear. One chord tone on beat 2 and one on beat 4, round a backdoor ii V. Tap your foot on 2 and 4 as you listen.

## Play

Beats 2 and 4 only; the rest is free. In the jazz blues, remember that bars 4, 11 and 12 change chord on beat 3, so the note on 4 belongs to the second chord: C7 in bar 4, A7alt in bar 11, G7 in bar 12.

exercises.title: Backdoor, beats 2 and 4
exercises.instructions: Fm7, Bb7, Cmaj7, Cmaj7. A chord tone on beat 2 and on beat 4 of each bar. Fm7 is F A flat C E flat, B flat 7 is B flat D F A flat, Cmaj7 is C E G B.

exercises.title: A minor turnaround, 2 and 4
exercises.instructions: Cm7, Am7b5, Dm7b5, G7alt, one chord a bar. A chord tone on beats 2 and 4. Each chord is new, so name its notes as you reach it.

exercises.title: The jazz blues, 2 and 4
exercises.instructions: Twelve bars, a chord tone on beats 2 and 4. In bars 4, 11 and 12 the chord changes on beat 3, so beat 4 belongs to the second chord: C7, A7alt and G7.

lessons.title: Minor scales and the slide
lessons.summary: Dorian, locrian and altered over minor chords, and a dorian vamp that slides up a half step.
lessons.explanation:
## Read

Minor is not one scale. Over a minor seventh chord you usually play dorian, with its raised sixth; over a minor seventh flat five you play locrian; over an altered dominant you play the altered scale, with every colour note in it. A minor tune moves between them.

The hardest part is the slide, such as D dorian a half step up to E flat dorian. The shape is the same and every note moves up a half step.

## Hear

Press Hear. Locrian over Am7b5, altered over D7alt, dorian over Gm7: one run of four notes for each, joined into a line.

## Play

Sixteen bars of dorian, with the slide up a half step at bar 9; a bossa minor ii V i; and the minor circle of fifths. Name the scale of each bar to yourself as it comes, and read a chord ahead.

exercises.title: Dorian, then a half step up
exercises.instructions: Sixteen bars: D dorian over Dm7 for eight bars, then E flat dorian over E flat m7 for eight. The white keys give D dorian. For E flat dorian, every note moves up a half step.

exercises.title: A minor ii V i
exercises.instructions: Am7, Bm7b5, E7alt, Am7. A dorian, B locrian, E altered, then A dorian again. Four bars, a different scale in each of the middle two.

exercises.title: The minor circle
exercises.instructions: Cm7, F7, Bbmaj7, Ebmaj7, Am7b5, D7alt, Gm7, Gm7. Dorian, mixolydian, two major scales, locrian, altered, dorian. Eight bars of the road a minor tune drives down.
